explanation: OEIS A159829 (Krug): are there infinitely many primes of the form n^k + m^k + 1 for k > 2? The formal statement asserts that for each k ≥ 3 the set of such primes (n, m ≥ 1) is infinite. I see no algebraic factorisation or local obstruction making this trivially false, so this is a reasonable, open, positive reading. Faithful.
